बडवा बडवा, f. a mare; the nymph
Aśvinī or the personification of the asterism repre-
sented by a horse's head; a female slave.
—बड-
वाग्नि (˚वा-अग्˚), इस्, or बडवानल (˚वा-अन्˚), अस्,
m. submarine fire; (in mythology) a being consisting
of flame but with the head of a mare, fabled to have
sprung from the thighs of Urvā and to have been
received by the ocean.
—बडवा-मुख, अस्, m.
submarine fire; (अम्), n. the infernal regions.
—ब-
डवा-सुत, औ, m. du. the two sons of Aśvinī, (see
अश्विन्, अश्विनी-कुमार.)
—बडवा-हृत (?), अस्,
m. the paramour of a female slave, a slave.
बडा बडा or बऌआ, ind., Ved. = बट्, q. v.
बडाह बडाह, अस्, m., N. of a prince.

बाड् बाड् (according to Vopa-deva वाड्),
cl. 1. A. बाडते, बाडितुम्, to bathe, dive;
to emerge; [cf. Gr. Βαλανεῖον: Lat. balneum:
Old Germ. bad, ‘a bath;’ badôn, ‘to bathe.’]

बाडीर बाडीर, अस्, m. a servant, a hired
labourer.
